A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding material can be reliably matched throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments in Section 6 and Appendix C, plus linear-regression simulation results in Appendix B.4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original classification experiments and the 1,000-run simulation results in Appendix B.4.

M1.justification: The bi-level optimization, objectives, hyper-gradients, and adaptations to existing methods are unchanged. Algorithm 1 newly specifies zero initialization of its existing momentum variable; this supplies an omitted detail rather than establishing a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Waterbirds, CelebA, the same binary MultiNLI task, and the same linear-regression simulation scenarios. No dataset, domain, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 2 and Tables 1–3 retain GW-ERM, SUBG, DFR, GDRO, and JTT, each compared with its optimized-weight counterpart. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same splits, sample sizes, ResNet50/BERT configurations, last-layer retraining, preprocessing, hyperparameter searches, and accuracy metrics. The simulation settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The CelebA sample-size analysis in Figure 3, Waterbirds regularization sensitivity in Figure 4, and simulation-versus-approximation analysis in Appendix B.4/Figure 5 are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report five experimental runs, standard errors, paired one-sided t-tests, and 90% confidence intervals for performance differences. Appendix B.4 retains 1,000 simulation runs and 95% confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain all numerical results and significance markers, and the plotted results are unchanged. For example, optimized GW-ERM's Waterbirds weighted average accuracy remains 91.998% in Table 1.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2, Equation 32 corrects the second sample-covariance expression from the group-1 matrix divided by n0 to the group-0 matrix divided by n0. This repairs a mathematical index error; assumptions and final bias–variance and optimal-weight formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that finite samples make standard importance weights suboptimal and that bi-level weight optimization improves existing methods for last-layer retraining.

C2.justification: Both retain the bias–variance interpretation, explanations of small-validation-set overfitting and JTT's CelebA failure, computational limitations of full-network retraining, and absence of formal convergence guarantees.

D1.justification: v2 adds an open-source implementation hyperlink in the introduction and explicitly specifies u0,g = 0 in Algorithm 1. These improve access information and implementation completeness; Appendix E's existing settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 changes its characterization of Cui et al. (2019) and Wen et al. (2020) from weighting by effective sample size to weighting by the number of available datapoints. The cited works and broader positioning remain unchanged; Nam et al. (2022) receives only a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammatical and wording corrections, adjusts mathematical typography, and replaces the preprint header with the ICLR 2025 publication header. Section ordering and the organization of Appendices A–E remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–4 retain their graphics, captions, structure, and placement. The page layout is preserved apart from incidental text reflow accompanying editorial changes.

improvement.justification: The new implementation link and explicit momentum initialization improve reproducibility documentation, while the Equation 32 correction and copyediting improve precision. These are limited benefits: the empirical evidence, central analysis, and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
